parsed.explanation: No trans-specific criminal statute, border rule, facility ban or custody practice is documented, and same-sex conduct has been lawful since 1998 — so the operative exposure is not state criminalisation but documented societal hostility combined with unreliable recourse. The dossier records frequent anti-LGBT violence and discrimination, a near-300% rise in attacks after the 2014 propaganda law, high stigma 'particularly from law enforcement', police blackmail of LGBTQ people via social/dating platforms, an MP calling for pride marchers to be beaten, and collapse of the capital's queer public life. No anti-discrimination or hate-crime protection exists, so an outed visitor has little realistic remedy. The pending 2026 bill and the 2020/2021 removal of gender recognition are resident-facing, but they confirm an actively deteriorating institutional climate. Elevated Risk, not severe: nothing shows organised state targeting of gender-nonconforming visitors.

entry_documents.exposure: No documented border practice targeting trans visitors; no reported marker-mismatch questioning, secondary screening or refusal of entry.
entry_documents.interaction: Visitor documents are home-issued; no domestic recognition process is engaged at the border on the record.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Police blackmail of LGBTQ people via social media and dating sites (2018), demanding roughly US$70–500; enforcement stigma documented in 2025 monitoring.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Not documented; no effective complaint channel described.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Dating/social platforms are a documented extortion vector that a lone visitor using apps would enter directly; police are the documented source of the pressure.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Placement and treatment of trans detainees is expressly unsourced in the dossier.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Cannot be assessed; no evidence either of a birth-sex placement rule reaching visitors or of a protective protocol.

care_services.exposure: Transition-related care domestically gated below age 25 (2024 amendment); a 2026 first-reading bill would bar gender-affirming care entirely. No documented refusal of emergency or routine care to foreign visitors.
care_services.interaction: Resident-facing gate; a visitor relying on home prescriptions has no documented continuity guarantee but no documented denial either.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Anti-LGBT legislative pushes in 2025 accompanied by parliamentary homophobic/transphobic rhetoric; 2019 MP call for pride participants to be beaten; child-protection 'propaganda' restrictions with undefined terms; 2026 bill passed first reading.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Some MPs condemned the 2019 remark; no institutional protection documented.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Rhetoric legitimises street-level hostility and discourages reporting, but no rule is shown operating against visitors.

minors_guardians.exposure: Draft law passed at first reading would restrict care and marker change for minors; care already gated below 25. No documented visitor-facing enforcement against a trans adult travelling with a minor.
minors_guardians.interaction: A trans guardian accompanying a minor faces no documented border or custody rule; exposure is climate, not operative practice.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Frequent reports of discrimination and violence against LGBTQ people; near-300% rise in attacks after the 2014 propaganda law; high stigma, especially from law enforcement; public queer life contracted to nothing in the capital.
street_violence_police_response.protection: No hate-crime or non-discrimination statute; no documented prosecution of anti-LGBT attackers.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Absent a working remedy, an outed visitor assaulted or extorted has little realistic recourse, and police are themselves a documented stigma source.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No anti-discrimination law, no legal gender recognition since 2021, no documented complaint mechanism producing outcomes for LGBTQ victims.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Recourse is effectively absent, so harms compound rather than being corrected.

anchor_checks.comparison: Vellandra documents a routine, traveller-facing entry bar, detention at the border and no effective appeal; this dossier documents no entry rule or refusal practice at all. The state machinery reaching visitors is plainly harsher there, so this jurisdiction sits above that anchor on the exposure side, though its street hostility is better documented.

Kestrel Isles documents recurring secondary screening, refused admission and humiliating searches of trans travellers — a universal-exposure border practice. Here no border friction is documented; the risk is societal and police-level rather than at the frontier, placing this jurisdiction slightly below Kestrel on severity of a specific encounter but without any comparable remedy.

Meridia's officers are trained, appeals are heard by a tribunal and unlawful detention draws compensation. This dossier has no anti-discrimination statute, no functioning remedy and police documented as extorting LGBTQ people, so it is materially lower — protections are absent, not merely uneven.

parsed.synthesis: The operative regime has no trans-specific criminal offence, no documented border or facility rule, and no evidence of organised state targeting of gender-nonconforming visitors; pending and resident-facing measures (2020/2021 removal of recognition, age-25 care floor, 2026 first-reading bill) confirm a deteriorating institutional climate rather than a traveller-facing prohibition. What the record does document is hostility the visitor cannot escape through paperwork: frequent anti-LGBT violence, parliamentary rhetoric endorsing it, police stigma and documented blackmail of LGBTQ people through dating and social platforms, and no anti-discrimination or hate-crime recourse. The tier-3 exposure — hostility with thin or no remedy — plus a dated tier-2 police-extortion practice sets the rating in the Elevated band, above operational exclusion regimes and well below jurisdictions where remedies actually work.
